All three full-resolution 1024x1024 renders inspected, plus magnified garment/lapel crops.

The reviewer's raw pixel numbers are accurate — garment dark-pixel means measure (24.9,23.3,23.0), (32.6,29.5,27.0), (25.5,24.7,23.4) at value ~0.10-0.13 — but the inference drawn from them does not survive calibration.

1. Saturation screen exonerates the item. `saturation_screen.json` groups on the `coloring` axis; deep_jewel has median 0.1628, min 0.1107, max 0.2117, and `outlier_count: 0` (deviation threshold 0.5). Computing this item's mean saturation directly across its three seeds gives 0.1296 — below the group median but comfortably inside the group's range, ranked 12th of 43 deep_jewel items, with 11 items scoring lower. Per the stated rule, a low absolute number is not evidence; only a value well below its own group's median is, and 0.1296 vs 0.1628 is not that. The screen flagged nothing here.

2. Peer items with lower saturation are not held. The entire low tail of deep_jewel is the `reflected_color` accent subgroup, i.e. this item's own subgroup: `rounded_soft_deep_jewel_crisp_shape_shadow_reflected_color` (0.1151) and `broken_dry_deep_jewel_fine_tonal_hatching_reflected_color` (0.1242) both score lower than case_099, and their garments are equally or more neutral — P7000277 renders a fully graphite, near-monochrome garment with dark-pixel mean flatter than case_099's. The neutral-black garment is a systematic property of deep_jewel x reflected_color in this run, not a case_099-specific coloring failure. For contrast, deep_jewel x controlled_rim (P7000007) does render a true emerald blazer, hue ~176 deg, sat 0.336 — so the rig is capable, and the split tracks the accent_light factor, not this item.

3. The item's own catalog prompt licenses the observed result: "filled with deep jewel color separated by dark neutrals and small high-value accents". A predominantly dark-neutral garment is inside the specification, not outside it. The darks are also not strictly hueless — satP95 ~0.4, and at full resolution the inner tee reads a distinctly cool navy (28.2,26.6,30.5) against a warmer blazer black (15.5,14.8,13.8) in seed 1001, i.e. local colour separation is present.

4. The secondary claims are thumbnail artifacts and are refuted at full resolution. The lapel/shoulder and sleeve contours show clearly broken, gappy dry-brush interruptions — broken_dry is plainly readable. Sleeve and skirt-pleat modelling shows the glazed plane transitions and luminous overlap of transparent_glaze. The contact sheet's own crib excludes only `accent_light` as unreadable at sheet density, not linework or shading, so writing those two off as "unreadable against the flat opaque black fill" was a density limitation, not a render property.

The hold rests on treating a low-but-in-range saturation value as a defect — exactly the calibration error the screen exists to catch — reinforced by two readability claims that dissolve at full size. Defect does not hold.

The core claim -- "no contour line is resolvable, the garment edge is a soft painted step from bg 180 into ~100-120 olive" -- is false at full resolution. Seeds 1001 and 2002 both show a continuous 1-2 px dark contour line around the entire garment silhouette, neckline, cuffs and every finger; that width is precisely why it disappeared at contact-sheet scale. Pixel scans across the left sleeve edge of P7000655 are non-monotonic, i.e. a drawn line rather than a painted step: row 600 goes 179,173,159 (bg) -> 86,77,56 (line trough) -> 131,117,88 (olive fill); row 500 goes 188,182,172 -> 112,103,85 -> 130,117,94; row 700 goes 184,178,167 -> 105,99,85 -> 142,128,107. The trough sits ~90 levels below bg AND ~45 levels below the fill it borders. Zoomed crops show the taper explicitly (line thins to nothing at the shoulder, thickens through the elbow fold and fingertips), so fine_tapered is rendering as intended. fine_tonal_hatching is also clearly present as fine parallel diagonal strokes on chest, sleeves and skirt in both seeds.

Secondary observation partly confirmed but not disqualifying: seed 3003 (P7000657) does have pure-255 side bars, content spanning columns 144-880 only. At full size this reads as a deliberate matted/framed painting reproduction with a thin white margin on all four sides, not a broken aspect fit. That seed is the most painterly of the three but still has an edge line (trough ~99-105 against a 115-130 fill); it is 1 of 3 seeds while the other 2 render the axis cleanly.

Saturation was not the concern, but saturation_screen.json reports outlier_total 0, and this item's own group (warm_earth) has the highest median of any palette group at 0.2194 (range 0.1838-0.2716) with 0 outliers, so there is no saturation evidence either.
